name: Cóiced

attributes.attribute: the fifth province and a cosmological idea
a province formed near the middle of Ireland

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cóiced is an Irish mythic theme bound to the island's provinces. Its word has the sense of a fifth. Three of those lands were lines drawn on a map. What was east lay in Leinster, Munster in the southwest, and west in Ireland. The fifth, Ulster in the north, and the last, Mide-Of the two excels as a true concept. It posed as the middle of the island, often said to rest at the hill named Uisneach or on the rock there titled the Divisions. In olden years the area of Meath was planted near the centre of the land, while the haze poetic of the old splits never went little.

okr.objective: Cóiced names the five provinces of ancient Ireland.
key_results: The term Cóiced means a fifth.
Leinster, Munster, Connacht, and Ulster were the four geographic provinces.
Mide or Meath was the fifth province as a cosmological idea.
Its center was the hill of Uisneach with the Stone of Divisions.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
